tests.name: Sun / Earth topocentric az, el
tests.reference: SPICE (DE440, MOON_ME, LT+S) direct evaluation at 24 random off-grid epochs × 4 sites
tests.result: max error 0.00009° (includes hourly linear interpolation and Float32 storage)
tests.detail: The reference is SPICE itself at the exact epoch; JPL Horizons cross-check not yet run.

tests.name: Horizon algorithm vs analytic cases
tests.reference: Bare-sphere dip angle (closed form); Gaussian hill vs 2 m brute-force 3-D scan
tests.result: worst error 0.00035°: bare sphere z=0 m: -0.0002° vs dip 0.0000°; bare sphere z=2 m: -0.0869° vs dip -0.0869°; bare sphere z=10 m: -0.1944° vs dip -0.1944°; bare sphere z=50 m: -0.4347° vs dip -0.4347°; Gaussian hill (H=1500 m, 14 km) z=2 m: 5.9423° vs brute 5.9426°; Gaussian hill (H=1500 m, 14 km) z=10 m: 5.9092° vs brute 5.9096°

tests.name: Convergence: azimuth resolution and reach
tests.reference: Same site and 29.5-day window re-run at 180/360/720/1440 azimuths and 35/100/200/300 km
tests.result: Coarse settings (180 az, 35 km) change the sunlit % by up to 5.8 points vs this app at the largest-effect site
tests.detail: Curves are shown below the table.

tests.name: Atlas vs point engine
tests.reference: 500 random cells × 6 azimuths across all 10 regions (Sun layer, 2 m)
tests.detail: Each cell is evaluated against its own region's terrain tiles (overlapping regions can otherwise pick different tiles at their shared edge). Both come from the same march code; this guards the bake pipeline, bit layout and region/cell indexing (the cell latitude and longitude are re-derived independently).

tests.name: Long-term average illumination and Earth visibility
tests.reference: PGDA AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (Sun) and _EARTH, 720 points at 85–90°S; ours = 2-hourly 2026–2044, any part of the disc visible, z = 0
tests.threshold: |bias| < 2 points and r > 0.95, Sun and Earth
tests.result: Sun: bias -0.74 pts, RMSE 4.45, r = 0.954 (r = 0.939 excluding permanently-dark pairs, n = 662). Earth: bias -0.88 pts, RMSE 5.21, r = 0.985 (r = 0.964 excl. dark, n = 488)
tests.detail: Not independent of this app’s terrain (same LOLA source) but independent in code and method: PGDA used its own 60 m DEM and horizon code. Differences include 60 m vs 20/40 m terrain, nearest-pixel sampling and a 19- vs 18.6-year span.

tests.name: Independent time-specific check (LROC WAC frames)
tests.reference: 12 WAC polar movie frames at their UTC (one per ~30 days, fixed rule), 1500 points within 38 km of the pole; image lit = per-frame Otsu DN threshold; predicted lit = Sun disc > 50%, z = 0
tests.threshold: pooled MCC > 0.6; mirrored-azimuth and +7-day-shift controls each < 0.3
tests.result: pooled MCC = 0.815 (mean of frames 0.822); controls: mirrored azimuth 0.246, date +7 d 0.147. With a fixed DN > 10 threshold instead of Otsu: 0.907. Orientation scan best = identity (0.815)
tests.detail: Frames are uncontrolled mosaics (geolocation can be off by a few hundred metres) and a few minutes of orbit time long. The image orientation was fixed from the time-averaged maps (see prep_imagery.py), not tuned on these frames.

tests.name: Performance budget
tests.reference: Node v24.22.3, arm64, single thread (browser worker figures will differ; measure on target devices)
tests.result: horizon median 45 ms (1440 az, 300 km); height slider 0.03 ms; 7-day analysis 1 ms; 19-year context 47 ms

tests.name: Exact mast height: obstruction envelope
tests.reference: Full re-march with the observer physically raised to each height (exact 3-D elevation)
tests.result: envelope worst error 0.00000°; a quadratic fit through the baked 0/5/20 m layers was off by up to 2.312° on the same rays

tests.name: Exploratory: published per-site sunlight days (Wueller et al. 2026)
tests.reference: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17084058 SunDays26–32, 78 Artemis III sites × 7 midsummers (n=546)
tests.result: INCONCLUSIVE. Spearman ρ = 0.12 / 0.25 against two pre-declared metrics of ours, but 5 of 78 sites share one identical 7-year sequence (the published counts saturate at a window length) and vary strongly by year while each site's own sunlit % is stable year to year. The published window cannot be reconstructed from the dataset description, so no agreement or disagreement is claimed.
tests.detail: Our metrics (declared before looking): longest continuous sunlit run and sunlit days within 30 days centred on 21 Dec, disc > 50%, 2 m.

tests.name: Imagery-derived illumination (LROC WAC percent-lit map)
tests.reference: WAC_POLE_ILL_PCT_SOUTH_100M, 3807 WAC images 2010-02-15 – 2011-02-05, 600 points at 88.7–90°S; ours = hourly over the same dates (2010 SPICE ephemeris), z = 0
tests.result: Sun disc > 50% visible: bias +0.09 pts, RMSE 2.72, r = 0.976 (excl. dark: 0.965). Sensitivity: any part visible: bias +1.88, r = 0.970; > 90% visible: bias -1.12, r = 0.977
tests.detail: Truly independent measurement: the reference is counted from real camera images, not modelled. WAC sampling is not uniform in time (documented bias), and the product thresholds image brightness, so some offset is expected.

gaps: Test 1 compares the browser interpolation to SPICE evaluated directly, not to JPL Horizons output; the SPICE kernels are the same source Horizons uses.

Test 5 caveats: the pooled correlation is helped by pooling regions of different brightness; per-domain Sun r is below 0.95 for pole 88.7–90°S (Sun r = 0.940, bias +0.4); Haworth (Sun r = 0.873, bias -2.5); Nobile Rim 1 (Sun r = 0.902, bias -2.0). Our Sun average is lower than PGDA's in 6 of 7 domains, and by 3.3 points in the brightest bin (PGDA 47.9% vs ours 44.6%, n = 46). The cause is not isolated (candidates: PGDA’s 60 m DEM and horizon reach, our 300 km reach, nearest-pixel sampling).

Test 6 caveats: the controls are low in the pooled data but not in every frame: 2 of 12 frames have a control MCC above 0.3 (max 0.41), because polar horizons have partly mirror-like structure. We predict more lit area than the thresholded image shows in 8 of 12 frames (by up to 5 points), consistent with a conservative image threshold and grazing-incidence pixels that are geometrically lit but dark in the image. The frames are uncontrolled mosaics; no registration correction was applied.
Test 9: the published SunDays metric saturates and is tied to a window we cannot reproduce, so it does not validate or invalidate our illumination numbers.
